ambiguities.text: The specification does not define behavior for empty code (zero-length bytecode) returned from init code
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume empty code is allowed since it has no first byte to check. Empty contracts remain valid and deployable. This aligns with existing EVM behavior.

ambiguities.text: The phrase 'exceptional abort' is used without defining whether it differs from standard out-of-gas behavior
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume exceptional abort behaves identically to out-of-gas: all remaining gas in the current call context is consumed, no state changes are persisted, and the operation fails.

implicit_assumptions.description: The block number is accurately known and correctly compared against HF_BLOCK for fork activation
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Clients could incorrectly apply or not apply the 0xEF restriction based on wrong fork detection

implicit_assumptions.description: Existing contracts in the account trie starting with 0xEF were deployed before the fork and are legitimate legacy code
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If 0xEF contracts exist pre-fork, they could be confused with valid EOF containers post-fork, causing parsing issues

implicit_assumptions.description: No mechanism exists to deploy 0xEF-prefixed code without going through CREATE/CREATE2 validation
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Bypassing the validation could allow invalid EOF containers that break future EOF parsing
